metadata.videoScript:
VIDEO SCRIPT: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS: DISAGREEING POLITELY
Grade: Grade 8 · Subject: ENGLISH

[0:00–0:20] HOOK
• Host: “Today we learn Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Conversational Skills: Disagreeing politely. Watch the example, then you try.”

[0:20–2:00] TEACH
• Euphemism = softer polite wording.
• Polite language shows respect.
• Practise short oral forms: riddles, proverbs, polite requests.

[2:00–4:00] WORKED EXAMPLE ON SCREEN
• “passed away” instead of “died”
• “washroom” instead of blunt toilet talk in formal settings
• “Please may I…?” for polite requests

[4:00–5:00] TRY THIS (PAUSE)

metadata.videoScript:
VIDEO SCRIPT: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 POLITE LANGUAGE: TELEPHONE ETIQUETTE
Grade: Grade 8 · Subject: ENGLISH

[0:00–0:20] HOOK
• Host: “Today we learn Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette. Watch the example, then you try.”

[0:20–2:00] TEACH
• Euphemism = softer polite wording.
• Polite language shows respect.
• Practise short oral forms: riddles, proverbs, polite requests.

[2:00–4:00] WORKED EXAMPLE ON SCREEN
• “passed away” instead of “died”
• “washroom” instead of blunt toilet talk in formal settings
• “Please may I…?” for polite requests

[4:00–5:00] TRY THIS (PAUSE)
• Write 5 direct sentences, then rewrite each with a euphemism / polite form.
• Role-play a market conversation using polite requests.
• Explain why polite language matters in school assemblies.

[5:00–5:30] REMEMBER + CTA
• Recap 3 bullets. “Now open Revision Quiz for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.”

— CBC Learn · Video Hub script aligned to lesson + revision

metadata.videoScript:
VIDEO SCRIPT: SQUARES AND SQUARE ROOTS
Grade: Grade 8 · Subject: MATHEMATICS

[0:00–0:20] HOOK
• Host: “Today we learn Squares and Square roots. Watch the example, then you try.”

[0:20–2:00] TEACH
• Perimeter = distance round a closed shape.
• Rectangle: P = 2(L + W).
• Square: P = 4 × side.
• Always use the same units (cm or m).

[2:00–4:00] WORKED EXAMPLE ON SCREEN
• Rectangle book: 18 cm × 13 cm → P = 62 cm.
• Door: 200 cm × 100 cm → P = 600 cm.
• Square tile side 15 cm → P = 60 cm.
• 9 m = 900 cm; 590 cm = 5 m 90 cm.

[4:00–5:00] TRY THIS (PAUSE)
• Find P of a rectangle 16 cm by 9 cm. Show both addition and 2(L+W).
• Find P of a square of side 12 cm.
• Convert 7 m to cm, then find P of a square of side 7 m in cm.

[5:00–5:30] REMEMBER + CTA
• Recap 3 bullets. “Now open Revision Quiz for Squares and Square roots.”

— CBC Learn · Video Hub script aligned to lesson + revision

Grade: Grade 8 · Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES

[0:00–0:20] HOOK
• Host: “Today we learn Plane Geometry. Watch the example, then you try.”

[0:20–2:00] TEACH
• Perimeter = distance round a closed shape.
• Rectangle: P = 2(L + W).
• Square: P = 4 × side.
• Always use the same units (cm or m).

[2:00–4:00] WORKED EXAMPLE ON SCREEN
• Rectangle book: 18 cm × 13 cm → P = 62 cm.
• Door: 200 cm × 100 cm → P = 600 cm.
• Square tile side 15 cm → P = 60 cm.
• 9 m = 900 cm; 590 cm = 5 m 90 cm.

[4:00–5:00] TRY THIS (PAUSE)
• Find P of a rectangle 16 cm by 9 cm. Show both addition and 2(L+W).
• Find P of a square of side 12 cm.
• Convert 7 m to cm, then find P of a square of side 7 m in cm.

[5:00–5:30] REMEMBER + CTA
• Recap 3 bullets. “Now open Revision Quiz for Plane Geometry.”

• Polite language shows respect.
• Practise short oral forms: riddles, proverbs, polite requests.

• Role-play a market conversation using polite requests.
• Explain why polite language matters in school assemblies.

• Host: “Today we learn Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs. Watch the example, then you try.”

[0:20–2:00] TEACH
• Euphemism = softer polite wording.
• Polite language shows respect.
• Practise short oral forms: riddles, proverbs, polite requests.

[2:00–4:00] WORKED EXAMPLE ON SCREEN
• “passed away” instead of “died”
• “washroom” instead of blunt toilet talk in formal settings
• “Please may I…?” for polite requests

[4:00–5:00] TRY THIS (PAUSE)
• Write 5 direct sentences, then rewrite each with a euphemism / polite form.
• Role-play a market conversation using polite requests.
• Explain why polite language matters in school assemblies.

[5:00–5:30] REMEMBER + CTA
• Recap 3 bullets. “Now open Revision Quiz for Reading 6.4.1 Oral literature: Songs.”

• Euphemism = softer polite wording.
• Polite language shows respect.
• Practise short oral forms: riddles, proverbs, polite requests.

• “passed away” instead of “died”
• “washroom” instead of blunt toilet talk in formal settings

• Write 5 direct sentences, then rewrite each with a euphemism / polite form.
• Role-play a market conversation using polite requests.
• Explain why polite language matters in school assemblies.

VIDEO SCRIPT: SQUARES AND SQUARE ROOTS
Grade: Grade 7 · Subject: MATHEMATICS

[0:00–0:20] HOOK
• Host: “Today we learn Squares and Square Roots. Watch the example, then you try.”

[0:20–2:00] TEACH
• Perimeter = distance round a closed shape.
• Rectangle: P = 2(L + W).
• Square: P = 4 × side.
• Always use the same units (cm or m).

[2:00–4:00] WORKED EXAMPLE ON SCREEN
• Rectangle book: 18 cm × 13 cm → P = 62 cm.
• Door: 200 cm × 100 cm → P = 600 cm.
• Square tile side 15 cm → P = 60 cm.
• 9 m = 900 cm; 590 cm = 5 m 90 cm.

[4:00–5:00] TRY THIS (PAUSE)
• Find P of a rectangle 16 cm by 9 cm. Show both addition and 2(L+W).
• Find P of a square of side 12 cm.
• Convert 7 m to cm, then find P of a square of side 7 m in cm.

[5:00–5:30] REMEMBER + CTA
• Recap 3 bullets. “Now open Revision Quiz for Squares and Square Roots.”

— CBC Learn · Video Hub script aligned to lesson + revision

VIDEO SCRIPT: MULTIPLICATION
Grade: Grade 5 · Subject: MATHEMATICS

[0:00–0:20] HOOK
• Host: “Today we learn Multiplication. Watch the example, then you try.”

[0:20–2:00] TEACH
• ×10 → add one zero; ×100 → add two zeros.
• Break 2-digit multipliers into tens + ones.
• Estimate by rounding to 10, then multiply.

[2:00–4:00] WORKED EXAMPLE ON SCREEN
• 24 × 10 = 240
• 23 × 14 = 322
• 18 × 100 = 1,800
• 48 × 19 ≈ 1,000

[4:00–5:00] TRY THIS (PAUSE)
• Work out: 16 × 10, 25 × 20, 33 × 30.
• Work out: 23 × 14 and 27 × 15. Show break-up.
• Work out: 18 × 100 and 42 × 100.

[5:00–5:30] REMEMBER + CTA
• Recap 3 bullets. “Now open Revision Quiz for Multiplication.”

— CBC Learn · Video Hub script aligned to lesson + revision

[0:00–0:20] HOOK
• Host: “Today we learn Plane Figures. Watch the example, then you try.”

[0:20–2:00] TEACH
• Perimeter = distance round a closed shape.
• Rectangle: P = 2(L + W).
• Square: P = 4 × side.
• Always use the same units (cm or m).

[2:00–4:00] WORKED EXAMPLE ON SCREEN
• Rectangle book: 18 cm × 13 cm → P = 62 cm.
• Door: 200 cm × 100 cm → P = 600 cm.
• Square tile side 15 cm → P = 60 cm.
• 9 m = 900 cm; 590 cm = 5 m 90 cm.

[4:00–5:00] TRY THIS (PAUSE)
• Find P of a rectangle 16 cm by 9 cm. Show both addition and 2(L+W).
• Find P of a square of side 12 cm.
• Convert 7 m to cm, then find P of a square of side 7 m in cm.

[5:00–5:30] REMEMBER + CTA
• Recap 3 bullets. “Now open Revision Quiz for Plane Figures.”

metadata.videoScript:
VIDEO SCRIPT: MULTIPLICATION
Grade: Grade 3 · Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES

[0:00–0:20] HOOK
• Host: “Today we learn Multiplication. Watch the example, then you try.”

[0:20–2:00] TEACH
• ×10 → add one zero; ×100 → add two zeros.
• Break 2-digit multipliers into tens + ones.
• Estimate by rounding to 10, then multiply.

[2:00–4:00] WORKED EXAMPLE ON SCREEN
• 24 × 10 = 240
• 23 × 14 = 322
• 18 × 100 = 1,800
• 48 × 19 ≈ 1,000

[4:00–5:00] TRY THIS (PAUSE)
• Work out: 16 × 10, 25 × 20, 33 × 30.
• Work out: 23 × 14 and 27 × 15. Show break-up.
• Work out: 18 × 100 and 42 × 100.

[5:00–5:30] REMEMBER + CTA
• Recap 3 bullets. “Now open Revision Quiz for Multiplication.”

— CBC Learn · Video Hub script aligned to lesson + revision

• Host: “Today we learn Polite SPEAKING. Watch the example, then you try.”

[0:20–2:00] TEACH
• Euphemism = softer polite wording.
• Polite language shows respect.
• Practise short oral forms: riddles, proverbs, polite requests.

[2:00–4:00] WORKED EXAMPLE ON SCREEN
• “passed away” instead of “died”
• “washroom” instead of blunt toilet talk in formal settings
• “Please may I…?” for polite requests

[4:00–5:00] TRY THIS (PAUSE)
• Write 5 direct sentences, then rewrite each with a euphemism / polite form.
• Role-play a market conversation using polite requests.
• Explain why polite language matters in school assemblies.

• Practise short oral forms: riddles, proverbs, polite requests.

• “Please may I…?” for polite requests

• Explain why polite language matters in school assemblies.
